designSummary: Two-arm cluster randomised trial, 11 practices, 12 months, analysis at consultation level accounting for clustering.
sampleSize: The network search suggests about 140 dental pain consultations per practice per year. With a baseline of 58 percent, an intracluster correlation of 0.06 as in the retrieved trial and 5 or 6 practices per arm, the design effect is about 9.3, giving roughly 80 percent power to detect a fall to 38 percent at two-sided alpha 0.05. A smaller fall, to 45 percent, would need about twice as many practices; if the observed intracluster correlation is higher, a neighbouring network would have to join.
primaryAnalysis: Mixed-effects logistic regression of prescription within 3 days on arm, with practice as a random effect and the stratification variables as fixed effects; small-sample corrected confidence intervals.
secondaryAnalysis: The same model for repeat consultation; emergency attendance and admission for dental infection reported as counts and rates per 1,000 consultations by arm, with the safety group's review; prescribing by deprivation fifth.
missingData: Outcomes come from coded records and are complete for consultations that are coded; coding completeness is checked against a sample of free-text notes in two practices.
multiplicity: One primary outcome; secondary and balancing measures are reported with intervals.
software: R (lme4 with small-sample corrections); analysis plan finalised before data extraction.
summary: About 80 percent power for 58 to 38 percent with 11 practices; smaller effects would need more practices.
